VIDEO.title: The HIDDEN Truth Behind Jesus & The Legion of Demons (and MORE) (Matthew 8:18-34)
VIDEO.series: The Gospel of Matthew Every Word (playlist of 58 videos)

SUMMARY: The teacher reads Matthew 8:18-34: a scribe and another disciple offer to follow Jesus; a great storm hits the boat while Jesus sleeps, and He rebukes the winds and sea; on the other side, in the region of the Gadarenes, He casts demons out of two men into a herd of swine.

The scribe wants to follow, unusually for a scribe, and Jesus warns that the Son of Man has nowhere to lay His head. The second man asks first to bury his father. The video takes Jesus' answer as hard as it sounds: 'leave the spiritually dead to bury their own physically dead.'

The storm is a seismos, the word for an earthquake, as at the cross and the empty tomb (27:54; 28:2). Jesus rebukes the sea the way He rebukes unclean spirits. The video says Jews saw the sea as the watery chaos of Genesis 1:2 and the abyss: a gateway to the underworld.

Geography matters: the far shore is the Gentile Decapolis, which the video links with Bashan, seen as the entry to the underworld. Using Deuteronomy 32:8, Psalm 82, Psalm 68 and Ephesians 4:8 (following Michael Heiser), it says Jesus is reclaiming the nations from rebel spiritual powers. 'Before the time' (8:29) shows the demons know their end is coming.

The lesson centers on Elisha's call in 1 Kings 19: he asked to kiss his parents, then sacrificed his oxen and followed with nothing to go back to. Luke adds, 'No one, after putting his hand to the plow and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God' (Luke 9:62).

To be a disciple, the only thing that comes first is doing the will of the Father (6:33; 7:21). There is no checklist of things to do first, and no room for double-mindedness, the hypocrite's condition.
QUOTES: Geography is important. The authors don't mention geography for no reason.
Jesus does not merely calm this storm. He appears to exorcise the storm.
In order to be a disciple of Jesus, the only thing that comes first is doing the will of the Father.
There is no checklist of things to do first before you decide to obey the will of the Father.
There is absolutely no room for this kind of double-mindedness.

method.p: The teacher's tip: when this study is done, go back and do a new study of the same passage. You should find more than one lesson every time, because God's word is that deep. Also read the parallels: Mark 4:35-5:20 and Luke 8:22-39.

LSB_QUOTES.text: The foxes have holes and the birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay His head.
What kind of a man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey Him?
No one, after putting his hand to the plow and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.

src.text: Then a scribe came and said to Him, “Teacher, I will follow You wherever You go.” And Jesus said to him, “The foxes have holes and the birds of the air have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay His head.”

lines.text: Scribes were experts in the Law of Moses; some served in the temple, the royal court, or the Sanhedrin. Unusually, this one wants to be a disciple.
If the rabbi is homeless, so are His disciples. For a scribe of standing, this was a hard word. Doing the Father's will may mean choosing it over a pillow.
This is Matthew's first use of 'Son of Man,' Jesus' favorite name for Himself (compare Daniel 7:13).

FOLLOW.title: Let the dead bury their own dead

src.text: And another of the disciples said to Him, “Lord, permit me first to go and bury my father.” But Jesus said to him, “Follow Me, and allow the dead to bury their own dead.”

lines.text: Do not soften it. The video reads: let the spiritually dead bury their own physically dead.
Many scholars think 'bury my father' was an idiom: let me stay until my father dies, then I will follow.
Chrysostom read the father as already dead: 'what can be more needful than to bury a father?' Even so, he says, 'it is far better to proclaim the kingdom' (Homilies on Matthew 27).

FOLLOW.title: He forsook the oxen and ran

left.text: Please let me kiss my father and my mother, then I will follow you.

right.text: Lord, permit me first to go and bury my father.

lines.text: Elijah passes by and throws his mantle on Elisha without stopping, so Elisha must decide at once; he has to run after him. (This is where we get 'passing the mantle.') Twelve pairs of oxen suggest Elisha was wealthy.

Elijah's reply, 'Go back again, for what have I done to you?', is mysterious. The video's proposal: Elijah puts the ball back in Elisha's court and trusts God, who had told him Elisha would replace him (19:16).
The text never says Elisha kissed his parents. He sacrificed the oxen, cooked them with the yoke, and gave the meat away. He 'burned the ships': nothing to go back to.

src.text: Another also said, “I will follow You, Lord, but first permit me to say farewell to those at home.” But Jesus said to him, “No one, after putting his hand to the plow and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.”

lines.text: Luke makes the Elisha connection clear: a plow and a farewell to home. What Elisha realized, every disciple must realize.
Jesus also says, 'none of you can be My disciple who does not give up all his own possessions' (Luke 14:33).

src.text: And behold, there arose a great storm on the sea, so that the boat was being covered with the waves; but Jesus Himself was sleeping. And they came to Him and got Him up, saying, “Save us, Lord; we are perishing!”

lines.text: The word for 'storm' is seismos, literally a shaking or earthquake. Matthew uses it again at the cross and the empty tomb, which suggests something spiritual is going on.
Why were seasoned fishermen so afraid? This was no ordinary storm.
Added: Jonah also slept through a great storm on the sea while the sailors feared they would perish (Jonah 1:4-6).

STORM.title: He rebuked the winds and the sea

left.text: Then He got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and it became perfectly calm.

right.text: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be quiet, and come out of him!”

lines.text: 'Rebuked' is the word Jesus uses with unclean spirits (Mark 1:25; 9:25; Luke 4:41). He does not merely calm this storm; He seems to exorcise it.
Mark has Him say to the sea, 'Silence! Be still' (Mark 4:39), the same 'be quiet' (phimoō) He says to the spirit in Mark 1:25.

src.text: And the earth was formless and void, and darkness was over the surface of the deep, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters.

lines.text: The video says Jews saw the Sea of Galilee, and the sea in general, as the watery chaos of Genesis 1:2. The sea was called the abyss: the gateway to the underworld where evil spirits dwelt.
Only God rules the sea in Israel's songs: 'When its waves rise, You still them' (Psalm 89:9). 'He caused the storm to stand still' (Psalm 107:29). So: 'What kind of a man is this?' (8:27).

src.text: And when He came to the other side, into the region of the Gadarenes, two men who were demon-possessed met Him as they were coming out of the tombs. They were so extremely violent that no one could pass by that way. And behold, they cried out, saying, “What do we have to do with You, Son of God? Have You come here to torment us before the time?”

lines.text: In Second Temple Judaism demons were 'unclean spirits.' The video says many Jews thought they came from the realm of the dead, and like corpses they were unclean. Jesus removes that uncleanness from the men.
In Luke they plead 'not to command them to go away into the abyss' (Luke 8:31): back where they came from. 'Before the time' means the end the demons know is coming.
Mark: 'My name is Legion; for we are many' (Mark 5:9). A Roman legion was about 5,000 soldiers.

src.text: When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, / When He separated the sons of man, / He set the boundaries of the peoples / According to the number of the sons of Israel. / For Yahweh’s portion is His people; / Jacob is the allotment of His inheritance.

lines.text: The video reads 'sons of God' in verse 8 (see Careful reading). With Michael Heiser, it says these sons of God were members of God's divine council who were given the nations, failed them (Psalm 82) and let the nations worship them: demons. Until Jesus, these borders were not crossed.
Moses: 'They sacrificed to demons who were not God' (Deuteronomy 32:17). Paul: 'the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons' (1 Corinthians 10:20).

BASHAN.title: He led captive a host of captives

left.text: A mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan; / A mountain of many peaks is the mountain of Bashan. / Why do you look with envy, O mountains with many peaks, / At the mountain which God has prized for His habitation?

right.text: When He ascended on high, / He led captive a host of captives, / And He gave gifts to men.

lines.text: The east shore is Gentile land, the Decapolis, which the video links with Bashan, seen as the entry point of the underworld. Crossing the lake, Jesus crosses the abyss into enemy ground.

Paul quotes Psalm 68 for Christ's triumph. The video: the Lord invades Bashan, takes prisoners, and reclaims it, undoing the division of the nations in Deuteronomy 32. Jesus casts out a whole legion and stills the sea.
Paul says the rulers of this age did not understand God's wisdom, 'for if they had understood it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory' (1 Corinthians 2:8).

PEOPLE.name: Elijah and Elisha

PEOPLE.name: The disciples

TERMS.def: An expert in the Law; some served in the temple, at court, or on the Sanhedrin.
Jesus' favorite title for Himself, drawn from Daniel 7:13-14.
A shaking or earthquake; Matthew's word for the storm (8:24).
The deep; in Jewish thought, the prison of evil spirits (Luke 8:31; Revelation 20:3).
The New Testament's other name for demons (Mark 1:23; 5:2).
God's heavenly assembly (Psalm 82:1). The video, following Michael Heiser, reads the 'sons of God' as its members.
The fertile highlands north-east of the Sea of Galilee (roughly the Golan and Hauran), famous for its bulls and oaks.
From Elijah throwing his cloak on Elisha (1 Kings 19:19): a call and an anointing.
Divided in loyalty; 'unstable in all his ways' (James 1:8).

WORDS.gloss: To rebuke; used of demons and fever too.
Legion: a Roman unit of about 5,000 soldiers.

BACKGROUND.p: The Sea of Galilee lies about 210 m below sea level, ringed by hills. Cool winds can drop through the valleys and whip up violent storms with little warning.
Matthew says 'Gadarenes,' Mark and Luke 'Gerasenes,' and some manuscripts 'Gergesenes.' Gadara was a nearby Decapolis city; Kursi on the east shore is the traditional site.
Pigs were unclean to Jews (Leviticus 11:7), but the Greek cities east of the lake raised them. A large herd marks this as Gentile land.
Touching a corpse or a grave made a person unclean (Numbers 19:16). Men living among the tombs were as cut off as they could be.

WITNESSES.text: And surely it is far better to proclaim the kingdom, and draw back others from death, than to bury the dead body, that is nothing advantaged thereby;
WITNESSES.src: Homilies on Matthew 27, on 8:21-22. Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, series 1, vol. 10 (public domain).

WITNESSES.text: That is, His power to rebuke when awakened they knew, but that He could do so even sleeping, they knew not as yet.
WITNESSES.src: Homilies on Matthew 28, on 8:24-26. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).

WITNESSES.text: Everywhere they have labored to drive men to dismay, and everywhere they rejoice in destruction.
WITNESSES.src: Homilies on Matthew 28, on 8:32. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).

DEBATES.p: Many scholars (and the video) read 'bury my father' as 'wait until he dies.' Others, like Chrysostom, take it literally: even a funeral must not come before following Jesus.

DEBATES.h: Why did the demons live in tombs?
DEBATES.p: The video: many Jews thought unclean spirits came from the realm of the dead (an idea found in 1 Enoch). Chrysostom rejected the idea that 'the souls of the dead become demons.'

DEBATES.h: 'Sons of God' and the divine council
DEBATES.p: The video follows Michael Heiser's reading of Deuteronomy 32:8 and Psalm 82: rebel heavenly beings over the nations. Others read Psalm 82's 'gods' as human judges (compare John 10:34-35).
Matthew has two; Mark and Luke tell of one. Many think Mark and Luke focus on the one who spoke or who later preached in the Decapolis (Mark 5:20).

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: Deuteronomy 32:8 reads 'the sons of Israel' in the LSB. The video's 'sons of God' follows the Dead Sea Scrolls and the Greek Old Testament, which some newer translations adopt. Both readings exist; the video's argument depends on the second.

Psalm 68:15-16 says Bashan's many-peaked mountain looks with envy at the mountain God chose for His home. The psalm does not say God ascends Bashan; that reading, of God conquering Bashan, is the video's (following Heiser).
Bashan lay mainly north-east of the lake (the Golan and Hauran). The Decapolis and Bashan overlap only in part, and Gadara sat south-east of the lake.
The video cites Ephesians 3, where 3:10 says God's wisdom is now made known to the rulers and authorities. The verse that says the rulers did not understand is 1 Corinthians 2:8.
1 Kings 19 is a classic call story, but not the first account of discipleship: Joshua was Moses' attendant long before (Exodus 24:13).

QUESTIONS: What is on your 'checklist of things to do first' before fully obeying God?
Elisha burned the plow and cooked the oxen. What would 'nothing to go back to' look like for you?
The disciples were experts on the water and still terrified. When has your experience failed you?
Jesus slept in the storm. What does that tell you about Him, and about fear?
The townspeople begged Jesus to leave after He freed two men. Why might people prefer their pigs to Jesus?
Where are you double-minded right now? What is one step toward a single focus?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: The lesson for the original audience: to be a disciple of Jesus, the only thing that comes first is doing the will of the Father. There is no checklist of things to do first. Seek first the kingdom (6:33); the one who enters is the one who does the Father's will (7:21). Jesus invites would-be disciples to the same realization Elisha had: forsake all and follow at once. Every day we face the choice to obey God or press pause to do what we think is better, and there is no room for double-mindedness, the condition of the hypocrite. Think about how this applies directly to your life so that you can do something about it.
APPLICATION_ADDED: Study note (added): name one thing you have told God 'first let me...' about. Like Elisha, take one concrete step this week that makes going back harder, and tell a friend so they can encourage you.

   [Background] Chrysostom read the father as already dead: 'what can be more needful than to bury a father?' Even so, he says, 'it is far better to proclaim the kingdom' (Homilies on Matthew 27).
3. Elisha's call · 1 Kings 19:19-21: He forsook the oxen and ran
   Elisha (1 Kings 19:20, LSB): "Please let me kiss my father and my mother, then I will follow you."
   The disciple (Matthew 8:21, LSB): "Lord, permit me first to go and bury my father."
   (video) Elijah passes by and throws his mantle on Elisha without stopping, so Elisha must decide at once; he has to run after him. (This is where we get 'passing the mantle.') Twelve pairs of oxen suggest Elisha was wealthy. (1 Kings 19:19)
   (video) Elijah's reply, 'Go back again, for what have I done to you?', is mysterious. The video's proposal: Elijah puts the ball back in Elisha's court and trusts God, who had told him Elisha would replace him (19:16). (1 Kings 19:16)
   (video) The text never says Elisha kissed his parents. He sacrificed the oxen, cooked them with the yoke, and gave the meat away. He 'burned the ships': nothing to go back to. (1 Kings 19:21)
4. Luke's addition · Luke 9:61-62: Hand to the plow
   No looking back Luke 9:61-62: "Another also said, “I will follow You, Lord, but first permit me to say farewell to those at home.” But Jesus said to him, “No one, after putting his hand to the plow and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.”" https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Luke+9:61-62
   (video) Luke makes the Elisha connection clear: a plow and a farewell to home. What Elisha realized, every disciple must realize.
   (video) Jesus also says, 'none of you can be My disciple who does not give up all his own possessions' (Luke 14:33). (Luke 14:28-33)

## The storm on the sea
1. The storm · Matthew 8:23-25: A great seismos
   Shaking Matthew 8:24-25: "And behold, there arose a great storm on the sea, so that the boat was being covered with the waves; but Jesus Himself was sleeping. And they came to Him and got Him up, saying, “Save us, Lord; we are perishing!”" https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Matthew+8:24-25
   (video) The word for 'storm' is seismos, literally a shaking or earthquake. Matthew uses it again at the cross and the empty tomb, which suggests something spiritual is going on. (Matthew 27:54; Matthew 28:2)
   (video) Why were seasoned fishermen so afraid? This was no ordinary storm.
   [Background] Added: Jonah also slept through a great storm on the sea while the sailors feared they would perish (Jonah 1:4-6). (Jonah 1:4-6)
2. The rebuke · Matthew 8:26: He rebuked the winds and the sea
   The sea (Matthew 8:26, LSB): "Then He got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and it became perfectly calm."
   A spirit (Mark 1:25, LSB): "And Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be quiet, and come out of him!”"
   (video) 'Rebuked' is the word Jesus uses with unclean spirits (Mark 1:25; 9:25; Luke 4:41). He does not merely calm this storm; He seems to exorcise it. (Mark 9:25; Luke 4:41)
   [Background] Mark has Him say to the sea, 'Silence! Be still' (Mark 4:39), the same 'be quiet' (phimoō) He says to the spirit in Mark 1:25. (Mark 4:39)
3. The deep · Genesis 1:2: Darkness over the deep
   Chaos Genesis 1:2: "And the earth was formless and void, and darkness was over the surface of the deep, and the Spirit of God was hovering over the surface of the waters." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Genesis+1:2
   (video) The video says Jews saw the Sea of Galilee, and the sea in general, as the watery chaos of Genesis 1:2. The sea was called the abyss: the gateway to the underworld where evil spirits dwelt.
   [Background] Only God rules the sea in Israel's songs: 'When its waves rise, You still them' (Psalm 89:9). 'He caused the storm to stand still' (Psalm 107:29). So: 'What kind of a man is this?' (8:27). (Psalm 89:9; Psalm 107:23-30)

## The other side: tombs, swine and Bashan
1. The tombs · Matthew 8:28-29: Before the time
   Unclean Matthew 8:28-29: "And when He came to the other side, into the region of the Gadarenes, two men who were demon-possessed met Him as they were coming out of the tombs. They were so extremely violent that no one could pass by that way. And behold, they cried out, saying, “What do we have to do with You, Son of God? Have You come here to torment us before the time?”" https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Matthew+8:28-29
   (video) In Second Temple Judaism demons were 'unclean spirits.' The video says many Jews thought they came from the realm of the dead, and like corpses they were unclean. Jesus removes that uncleanness from the men.
   (video) In Luke they plead 'not to command them to go away into the abyss' (Luke 8:31): back where they came from. 'Before the time' means the end the demons know is coming. (Luke 8:31)
   [Background] Mark: 'My name is Legion; for we are many' (Mark 5:9). A Roman legion was about 5,000 soldiers. (Mark 5:9)
2. The nations · Deuteronomy 32:8-9: The boundaries of the peoples
   Nations Deuteronomy 32:8-9: "When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, / When He separated the sons of man, / He set the boundaries of the peoples / According to the number of the sons of Israel. / For Yahweh’s portion is His people; / Jacob is the allotment of His inheritance." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Deuteronomy+32:8-9
   (video) The video reads 'sons of God' in verse 8 (see Careful reading). With Michael Heiser, it says these sons of God were members of God's divine council who were given the nations, failed them (Psalm 82) and let the nations worship them: demons. Until Jesus, these borders were not crossed. (Psalm 82:6-7)
   [Background] Moses: 'They sacrificed to demons who were not God' (Deuteronomy 32:17). Paul: 'the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons' (1 Corinthians 10:20). (Deuteronomy 32:17; 1 Corinthians 10:20)
3. Bashan · Psalm 68: He led captive a host of captives
   Psalm 68 (Psalm 68:15-16, LSB): "A mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan; / A mountain of many peaks is the mountain of Bashan. / Why do you look with envy, O mountains with many peaks, / At the mountain which God has prized for His habitation?"
   Paul (Ephesians 4:8, LSB): "When He ascended on high, / He led captive a host of captives, / And He gave gifts to men."
   (video) The east shore is Gentile land, the Decapolis, which the video links with Bashan, seen as the entry point of the underworld. Crossing the lake, Jesus crosses the abyss into enemy ground.
   (video) Paul quotes Psalm 68 for Christ's triumph. The video: the Lord invades Bashan, takes prisoners, and reclaims it, undoing the division of the nations in Deuteronomy 32. Jesus casts out a whole legion and stills the sea.
   [Background] Paul says the rulers of this age did not understand God's wisdom, 'for if they had understood it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory' (1 Corinthians 2:8). (1 Corinthians 2:8)

## Key people
- Jesus: Calls disciples to put the Father's will first, stills a storm, and drives out a legion of demons on Gentile ground. [Background] 'Son of Man' (8:20) is the name Jesus uses most for Himself.
- The scribe: A Torah expert who wants to follow Jesus, unusually; he must learn the cost. [Background] Matthew mentions a scribe 'who has become a disciple of the kingdom of heaven' (13:52).
- The would-be disciple: Wants first to bury his father; perhaps to wait until his father dies. [Background] Burying parents was a weighty duty in Judaism.
- Elijah and Elisha: The model of a call to discipleship: Elijah throws his mantle; Elisha leaves everything. [Background] Elisha later receives a double portion of Elijah's spirit (2 Kings 2:9-15).
- The disciples: Seasoned fishermen, terrified by a storm they should have known how to handle. [Background] 'You men of little faith' (8:26): Matthew's word for disciples who believe, but weakly (6:30; 14:31).
- The two demoniacs: From the tombs, so violent no one could pass; the demons know Jesus is the Son of God. [Background] Mark and Luke focus on one man, who then tells the Decapolis what Jesus did (Mark 5:20).
- Michael Heiser: Named in the video for reading the 'sons of God' as God's divine council. [Background] A biblical scholar (1963-2023) known for The Unseen Realm (2015).

## Places [Background]
- Capernaum: Jesus' base on the west shore, where the crossing likely began.
- Kursi: The traditional site of the miracle on the east shore, with a steep slope near the water; often linked with Gergesa.
- Gadara (named in the video): 'The region of the Gadarenes' (8:28): this Decapolis city controlled land toward the lake.
- Hippos: Another Decapolis city on the east shore.
- Tiberias: On the west shore, in Jewish Galilee.
- Magdala: Fishing town on the west shore.

## Key terms
- Scribe: An expert in the Law; some served in the temple, at court, or on the Sanhedrin.
- Son of Man: Jesus' favorite title for Himself, drawn from Daniel 7:13-14. [Background]
- Seismos: A shaking or earthquake; Matthew's word for the storm (8:24).
- Abyss: The deep; in Jewish thought, the prison of evil spirits (Luke 8:31; Revelation 20:3).
- Unclean spirits: The New Testament's other name for demons (Mark 1:23; 5:2).
- Divine council: God's heavenly assembly (Psalm 82:1). The video, following Michael Heiser, reads the 'sons of God' as its members.
- Bashan: The fertile highlands north-east of the Sea of Galilee (roughly the Golan and Hauran), famous for its bulls and oaks.
- Passing the mantle: From Elijah throwing his cloak on Elisha (1 Kings 19:19): a call and an anointing.
- Double-minded: Divided in loyalty; 'unstable in all his ways' (James 1:8).

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- Storms on the lake: The Sea of Galilee lies about 210 m below sea level, ringed by hills. Cool winds can drop through the valleys and whip up violent storms with little warning.
- Gadarenes, Gerasenes, Gergesenes: Matthew says 'Gadarenes,' Mark and Luke 'Gerasenes,' and some manuscripts 'Gergesenes.' Gadara was a nearby Decapolis city; Kursi on the east shore is the traditional site.
- Pigs in the Decapolis: Pigs were unclean to Jews (Leviticus 11:7), but the Greek cities east of the lake raised them. A large herd marks this as Gentile land.
- Tombs and the unclean: Touching a corpse or a grave made a person unclean (Numbers 19:16). Men living among the tombs were as cut off as they could be.

## Early witnesses [Background: sourced]
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 390): "And surely it is far better to proclaim the kingdom, and draw back others from death, than to bury the dead body, that is nothing advantaged thereby;" Homilies on Matthew 27, on 8:21-22. Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, series 1, vol. 10 (public domain).
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 390): "That is, His power to rebuke when awakened they knew, but that He could do so even sleeping, they knew not as yet." Homilies on Matthew 28, on 8:24-26. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 390): "Everywhere they have labored to drive men to dismay, and everywhere they rejoice in destruction." Homilies on Matthew 28, on 8:32. NPNF 1.10 (public domain).

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- Was the father already dead? Many scholars (and the video) read 'bury my father' as 'wait until he dies.' Others, like Chrysostom, take it literally: even a funeral must not come before following Jesus.
- Why did the demons live in tombs? The video: many Jews thought unclean spirits came from the realm of the dead (an idea found in 1 Enoch). Chrysostom rejected the idea that 'the souls of the dead become demons.'
- 'Sons of God' and the divine council The video follows Michael Heiser's reading of Deuteronomy 32:8 and Psalm 82: rebel heavenly beings over the nations. Others read Psalm 82's 'gods' as human judges (compare John 10:34-35).
- One demoniac or two? Matthew has two; Mark and Luke tell of one. Many think Mark and Luke focus on the one who spoke or who later preached in the Decapolis (Mark 5:20).

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- Deuteronomy 32:8 reads 'the sons of Israel' in the LSB. The video's 'sons of God' follows the Dead Sea Scrolls and the Greek Old Testament, which some newer translations adopt. Both readings exist; the video's argument depends on the second.
- Psalm 68:15-16 says Bashan's many-peaked mountain looks with envy at the mountain God chose for His home. The psalm does not say God ascends Bashan; that reading, of God conquering Bashan, is the video's (following Heiser).
- Bashan lay mainly north-east of the lake (the Golan and Hauran). The Decapolis and Bashan overlap only in part, and Gadara sat south-east of the lake.
- The video cites Ephesians 3, where 3:10 says God's wisdom is now made known to the rulers and authorities. The verse that says the rulers did not understand is 1 Corinthians 2:8.
- 1 Kings 19 is a classic call story, but not the first account of discipleship: Joshua was Moses' attendant long before (Exodus 24:13).

## Reflection and discussion questions
1. What is on your 'checklist of things to do first' before fully obeying God?
2. Elisha burned the plow and cooked the oxen. What would 'nothing to go back to' look like for you?
3. The disciples were experts on the water and still terrified. When has your experience failed you?
4. Jesus slept in the storm. What does that tell you about Him, and about fear?
5. The townspeople begged Jesus to leave after He freed two men. Why might people prefer their pigs to Jesus?
6. Where are you double-minded right now? What is one step toward a single focus?

## Application
- (video) The lesson for the original audience: to be a disciple of Jesus, the only thing that comes first is doing the will of the Father. There is no checklist of things to do first. Seek first the kingdom (6:33); the one who enters is the one who does the Father's will (7:21). Jesus invites would-be disciples to the same realization Elisha had: forsake all and follow at once. Every day we face the choice to obey God or press pause to do what we think is better, and there is no room for double-mindedness, the condition of the hypocrite. Think about how this applies directly to your life so that you can do something about it.
- Study note (added): name one thing you have told God 'first let me...' about. Like Elisha, take one concrete step this week that makes going back harder, and tell a friend so they can encourage you.
